## Summary

3.0.0 is the major release that follows client-go to v3. The Go module path is now `github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/v3`, what 2.x deprecated is removed, and HTTP mode serves only the GitLab instances its operator names. It fixes GHSA-fcj2-hj27-hj26, a server-side request forgery in legacy HTTP mode that affects every release from 1.1.0 through 2.7.5.

- HTTP mode refuses to start until `--gitlab-url` (or `GITLAB_URL`) names the instance, or instances, it serves (#407). A request that names an instance outside that list is refused, a deployment that publishes several requires the `GITLAB-URL` header (#407, #479), and a request that names none is no longer sent to `https://gitlab.com`.
- Outbound connections are checked after DNS resolution (#676, ADR-0022). Cloud metadata addresses are refused on every redirect and for every destination the operator did not name, and loopback and private addresses are refused for a destination a caller or a redirect chose. An address `--gitlab-url` names is never checked, so a self-managed GitLab on a private network keeps working.
- A redirect that leaves the configured instance, or drops to plain `http`, no longer carries the credential headers (#407).
- The self-updater and the setup wizard are gone (#336). The binary no longer contacts `api.github.com` at startup or fetches and runs code while it serves, and you upgrade it through the channel that installed it.
- Every setting this project defines is read as `GITLAB_MCP_<NAME>` (#412, #523). The old spellings still work in 3.0.0 and print a warning naming the new one; 3.1.0 stops reading them.
- Creating a push mirror (`project.mirror_add`) asks for confirmation, and the individual tool surface now lists only what the token's scopes can reach (#673). A stdio session whose token carries `read_api` without `api` is served the read-only surface, as HTTP mode already was (#505).
- OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs can be exported over OTLP, off by default (#337). The container image picks its transport from how it is started, stdio with `docker run -i` and HTTP without it, so client configurations no longer need `--http=false` (#410).

## Breaking changes

- The module path moves to `/v3` and client-go to v3 (#640). Feature flag strategy inputs split into a create shape and an update shape, as GitLab's API documents them, and the `approved` filter, which GitLab never documented, leaves the merge request lists.
- Removed (#641): `META_TOOLS`, its `GITLAB_MCP_` spelling, the `--meta-tools` flag and the `META_TOOLS` and `META-TOOLS` request headers (`GITLAB_MCP_TOOL_SURFACE` replaces them); `GITLAB_ENTERPRISE` (the tier is detected, or pinned with `GITLAB_MCP_TIER`); and the flat Datadog fields of the group Datadog output, whose `properties` object is now its only shape.
- Removed (#336): self-update (`AUTO_UPDATE` and its siblings), the `--setup` wizard and `--setup-mode`.
- HTTP mode does not start without `--gitlab-url` or `GITLAB_URL`. `--allow-any-gitlab-url` keeps per-request instance selection for a single-user local deployment, and is accepted only when `--http-addr` binds a loopback address or a unix socket (#645).
- A `.env` in the working directory no longer configures the server; it is reported at startup and not loaded (#407). The server loads `~/.gitlab-mcp-server.env` and the file `GITLAB_MCP_ENV_FILE` or `--env-file` names.
- A tool reads or writes a local file only inside the working directory, the system temporary directory and the directories `GITLAB_MCP_ALLOWED_UPLOAD_DIRS`, `GITLAB_MCP_ALLOWED_DOWNLOAD_DIRS` and `GITLAB_MCP_ALLOWED_IMPORT_DIRS` list, and over HTTP it names no local path at all (#407).
- A destination a caller or a redirect chose is refused on a private address until `--allow-private-instances` (`GITLAB_MCP_ALLOW_PRIVATE_INSTANCES`) is set (#676). Two deployments meet it: one using `--allow-any-gitlab-url` against a GitLab on a private address, and one whose public GitLab redirects downloads to object storage on a private address.
- `project.mirror_add` needs `confirm: true` from a client that cannot answer an elicitation prompt, unless `GITLAB_MCP_YOLO_MODE` is set (#673).

## Upgrading

1. HTTP deployments: pass `--gitlab-url` with every instance the deployment serves, or set `GITLAB_URL`. The published image names no instance, so `docker run` it with `-e GITLAB_URL=<url>`.
2. Replace `META_TOOLS` with `GITLAB_MCP_TOOL_SURFACE` (`dynamic`, the default, `meta` or `individual`), and `GITLAB_ENTERPRISE` with `GITLAB_MCP_TIER`, or leave the tier to detection.
3. Rename every other setting to its `GITLAB_MCP_` name now: the old names still work in 3.0.0, and 3.1.0 stops reading them. Configuration lists each name: <https://docs.jmrp.io/gitlab-mcp-server/configuration/#variable-naming>.
4. Move a working-directory `.env` to `~/.gitlab-mcp-server.env`, or point `GITLAB_MCP_ENV_FILE` at it.
5. If a tool reads or writes files outside the working directory, list those directories in the `GITLAB_MCP_ALLOWED_*_DIRS` variables.
6. 3.0.0 does not update itself. Later releases are installed through the channel that installed this one: npm, PyPI, NuGet, Homebrew, winget, a newer image tag, a newer Claude Desktop extension or a new release asset.
7. Code that imports the module uses `github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/v3`.

## Security

- Fixes [GHSA-fcj2-hj27-hj26](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/security/advisories/GHSA-fcj2-hj27-hj26) (high, CVSS 7.2, CWE-918): in legacy HTTP mode with no fixed GitLab URL, any client that could reach the endpoint chose the host the server sent requests to through the `GITLAB-URL` header, with any non-empty token. Every release from 1.1.0 through 2.7.5 is affected. The fix is the instance allow-list above (#407, #479, #645), and the outbound destination guard (#676) closes what was left of it. The 1.x and 2.x module paths carry no patched release, so upgrading to 3.0.0 or later is the remedy.
- Also fixed, from the September 2026 security audit (#407): the credential headers no longer follow a redirect off the instance, GitLab-authored text is quoted and escaped before it reaches the model, and the nesting of tool arguments and the size of GitLab's responses are bounded. None of these had an advisory of its own.
- The binaries no longer link `golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp`, which only the self-updater used and which GO-2026-5932 covers in every version (#336). Scanners that judge a binary by the modules it records still reported that advisory against 3.0.0 and 3.1.0, since the module stayed for one key derivation; 3.2.0 removes it from the build (#1122).
